FIDELITY: System2 workflows for Codex. NOTE: safety enforcement is INACTIVE until you review and trust the bundled hooks via /hooks; until then System2 runs advisory-only. On Codex the safety gates (enforce-lease, block-dangerous, protect-sensitive) are ADAPTED, never native: they are deterministic pre-execution blocks (modern deny schema: hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision=deny) ONLY once the guard is active — materialized to ~/.codex/hooks.json by `system2 codex init` and reviewed+trusted via /hooks; until then they are advisory-only, and an admin requirements.toml override can disable them immutably. budget is ADAPTED (a Stop-event report, not a block). format/typecheck are ADVISORY (skill instruction only). Even with hooks trusted, Codex hooks intercept shell commands and apply_patch-matched edits; they do NOT intercept WebSearch or other non-shell, non-MCP tools. Enforcement on Codex is therefore ADAPTED, never total. EMPTY-SCOPE (UNSCOPED) ROLES FAIL CLOSED: one or more roles carry an empty write_scope (read-only roles); when the hooks are trusted the lease BLOCKS every write for them. This is fail-closed enforcement, not a silent allow.

enforce-lease.mechanism: generated Node command hook (PreToolUse on apply_patch/Edit/Write and shell write-redirections): a write outside the active role's write_scope regex is hard-blocked (modern Codex deny schema on stdout: {"hookSpecificOutput":{"permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":R}}) BEFORE the tool runs — deterministic pre-execution block IFF the guard is active: materialized to ~/.codex/hooks.json by `system2 codex init` and reviewed+trusted via /hooks. It is ADAPTED, never native: enforcement is gated on the Codex trust model (untrusted or admin-disabled hooks never run, so System2 is advisory-only until trusted), and tool coverage is PARTIAL (shell + apply_patch/Edit/Write only — NOT WebSearch or other non-shell, non-MCP tools). The matcher is the proven lease algorithm from backends/_enforcement.build_lease_gate_source: path project-normalized (./ collapsed, .. resolved, ~/absolute rejected) and FAILS CLOSED on any escape, scope start-anchored (new RegExp("^(?:" + scope + ")")), OR-joined from the role allowlist; a role with an empty write_scope (read-only, e.g. code-reviewer) has EVERY write BLOCKED (fail-closed). The active role is read from SYSTEM2_ACTIVE_ROLE (in-session role-switch, adapted) and falls back to the default role. enforced:false, gated:true.

block-dangerous.mechanism: generated Node command hook (PreToolUse on shell): a command matching the backend-owned dangerous-command set is hard-blocked (modern Codex deny schema on stdout: {"hookSpecificOutput":{"permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":R}}) BEFORE execution — deterministic pre-execution block IFF the guard is active: materialized to ~/.codex/hooks.json by `system2 codex init` and reviewed+trusted via /hooks; advisory-only until trusted; partial tool coverage (shell only, not WebSearch/other). The matcher is the proven Claude dangerous-command set ported VERBATIM via backends/_enforcement.build_dangerous_command_patterns (flag-permutation _RM_RF_FLAGS: -rf/-fr/-r -f/--recursive --force, interior whitespace; rm -rf at / . .. ~, sudo rm -rf, chmod 777, git reset --hard, git push --force/-f to main/master, DROP TABLE, DELETE FROM without WHERE, mkfs, dd of=, shutdown, curl|sh). The command length is capped before matching and any internal error/timeout fails closed (exit 2). It is ADAPTED, never native: gated on the Codex trust model. enforced:false, gated:true.

protect-sensitive.mechanism: generated Node command hook (PreToolUse on shell and on apply_patch/Edit/Write): an edit path or slash-delimited shell path touching a backend-owned sensitive path (.env, .env.*, .ssh/, .git/, .aws/, id_rsa, *.pem, *.key, credentials, secrets, .netrc/.npmrc/.pypirc) is hard-blocked; bare relative shell arguments (for example `cat .env`) are not parsed as paths and remain advisory (modern Codex deny schema on stdout: {"hookSpecificOutput":{"permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":R}}) BEFORE the tool runs — deterministic pre-execution block IFF the guard is active: materialized to ~/.codex/hooks.json by `system2 codex init` and reviewed+trusted via /hooks; advisory-only until trusted; partial tool coverage (shell + apply_patch/Edit/Write only, not WebSearch/other). The matcher is the proven sensitive-file set ported VERBATIM via backends/_enforcement.build_sensitive_path_patterns (segment/basename-anchored regexes). It is ADAPTED, never native: gated on the Codex trust model. enforced:false, gated:true.

format.mechanism: orchestrator + per-role skill instruction block only, clearly labelled "ADVISORY — NOT ENFORCED ON CODEX (instruction only)": Codex has no post-edit formatter hook the compiler can wire deterministically, and the IR carries no per-language formatter command, so formatting is NOT enforced. The agent is instructed to format edited files. Making this native needs IR-enrichment (per-language formatter command) deferred this cycle.

typecheck.mechanism: orchestrator + per-role skill instruction block only, clearly labelled "ADVISORY — NOT ENFORCED ON CODEX (instruction only)": Codex has no post-edit type-check hook the compiler can wire deterministically, and the IR carries no per-language checker command, so type-checking is NOT enforced. The agent is instructed to type-check edited files. Making this native needs IR-enrichment deferred this cycle.

budget.mechanism: generated Node command hook (Stop/SubagentStop): the change budget (files touched, lines added/removed) is reported at turn end via the hook's systemMessage. This is a REPORT, not a block — a Stop-event hook cannot retroactively prevent edits, so it is adapted (a gated report), NOT native enforcement. enforced:false, gated:true.
